title: Installing a Single-Lever, Anti-Scald Shower Valve (Pressure-Balance) in a Bathroom

locations.name: Bathroom
locations.basis: Explicitly shown and discussed as the work area in the transcript

locations.name: Basement
locations.basis: Explicitly referenced as the place to turn off the water

summary: This Old House presents a step-by-step installation of a modern single-lever, pressure-balanced anti-scald shower valve to replace a failing old three-valve tub/shower setup. The episode covers diagnosing the risk of scalding due to pressure fluctuations, removing the old valve and surrounding tile, templating and cutting the wall for a new valve, dry-fitting and soldering copper connections, installing the trim plate and safety limit, and testing the finished shower for both temperature stability and leak-free operation, all while discussing code implications for anti-scald valves and permits when remodeling.
topics: tile removal and mud bed construction

sections.title: Problem identification: Old three-valve system and scald risk
sections.description: Richard explains how the old three-valve setup mixes hot and cold water at a single diverter and how pressure drops elsewhere in the house can cause sudden hot water inflow, creating a scald risk. The plan is to replace with a single-lever, pressure-balanced valve to stabilize temperature.

sections.title: Preparation and wall prep: cover plate, shutoff, and removal
concepts: template and witness lines for wall cutout
sections.description: To avoid retiling, a cover plate is used to conceal old valve openings. The water is shut off in the basement, and the old handles, escutcheons, and stems are removed with a handle puller. The wall opening is planned using a manufacturer template and witness lines to mark the cutout.

sections.title: Valve installation: dry-fit, soldering, and safety checks
sections.description: The single-lever pressure-balanced valve is dry-fitted in the wall, then the hot and cold supplies, shower head, and tub spout connections are prepared with cleaned fittings and flux before soldering. The spindle is removed and later reinstalled, and a leak test is performed after reassembly.

sections.title: Finish trim, setting temperature limit, and final test
concepts: gasket and putty for a watertight seal
sections.description: The trim plate and escutcheon are installed with a gasket and putty to seal the wall. A temperature limit is set using a screw and a thermometer to keep the shower output around 120 F or lower. The finish is tested with a shower run, including checks of the diverter function between tub and shower, and a safety-code discussion about anti-scald requirements and permits.
